lesson.title: Sort it into a table
lesson.subtitle: Rows, columns, headings, and one fact in each cell

video.title: Sort it into a table
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — the science teacher (main character)
Ms Amina Bello — the class teacher (cameo)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Our garden; Scraps of paper; Everywhere!. Mr Okafor beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Our class garden grew beans, maize and tomatoes. Every day, pupils wrote what they picked on scraps of paper. Now the scraps are everywhere!

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: sort data into a table, so it's easy to read and to count.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Rows go across: days; Columns go down: crops; A heading on each column.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Rows go across, columns go down
scenes.narration: A table sorts data into rows and columns. Rows go across, like the days of the week. Columns go down, like beans, maize and tomatoes. Each column has a heading.

scenes.visual: One big value: 6, Monday's beans: one fact, one cell.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Where a row meets a column, there's a cell. Each cell holds one fact: Monday, beans, six. One fact per cell, always.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Monday; Beans: 6; Maize: 2; Tomatoes: 4; The whole week at once.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here's one row of our garden table. On Monday we picked six beans, two maize cobs and four tomatoes. With a row for every day, we can see the whole week at once.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Biggest first; The best day at once; Or by name.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Tables are easy to sort. Put the biggest first, and you see the best day straight away. Or sort by name, from A to Z.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! In a table of pupils, what does one row show?

scenes.visual: Icon cards: A row: one pupil; A column: one fact.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: One pupil. Each row is one thing, and each column is one fact about it, like age or favourite colour.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Two facts in one cell; A Total row in the middle; Fixed: counts right.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some tables confuse computers. A cell with two facts, like three and five. A Total row in the middle. Fix them, and the computer counts right.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Looks fine; Tap a fix; Counts right.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, Mr Bello's marks table looks fine to us. But the computer counts the pupils wrong! Tap a fix, and watch its answer turn right.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. One cell says three and five: the beans and the tomatoes. What's wrong?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Rows across, columns down; A heading on each column; One fact in each cell. Takeaway bar: A tidy table is easy to read and to count.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Two facts in one cell: give beans and tomatoes a column each. Remember: rows go across, and columns go down. Every column needs a heading. And put one fact in each cell.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A table of your week; One row each day; Weather, and how you came. Mr Okafor beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: make a table of your week. One row for each day. Columns for the weather, and how you got to school.

checkpoints.prompt: In a table of pupils, what does one row show?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — each row is one pupil, and each column is one fact about them.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — in a table of pupils, each row is one pupil. The facts about them go in the columns.

checkpoints.prompt: One cell says “3 and 5”: the beans and the tomatoes. What's wrong?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — each cell holds one fact. Give beans and tomatoes a column each.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a computer can't count “3 and 5”. Put each fact in its own cell.
